simple.meaning: כְּתַב (kᵉthab) is a Hebrew action word meaning “write(-ten).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 8 times in Ezra, Daniel, beginning at Ezra 4:8. The surrounding contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to כְּתַב (H3790) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: כְּתַב (kᵉthab) / H3790 is traced through Ezra 4:8, Ezra 5:7, Ezra 5:10, Ezra 6:2 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Rehum the chancellor and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter against Jerusalem to Artaxerxes the king as follows,

timeline.evidenceText: Rehum the chancellor and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter against Jerusalem to Artaxerxes the king as follows,
They sent a letter to him, in which was written:
We asked them their names also, to inform you that we might write the names of the men who were at their head.
A scroll was found at Achmetha, in the palace that is in the province of Media, and in it this was written for a record:
In the same hour, the fingers of a man’s hand came out and wrote near the lamp stand on the plaster of the wall of the king’s palace. The king saw the part of the hand that wrote.
In the same hour, the fingers of a man’s hand came out and wrote near the lamp stand on the plaster of the wall of the king’s palace. The king saw the part of the hand that wrote.
“I make a decree that in all the dominion of my kingdom men tremble and fear before the God of Daniel;
In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon Daniel had a dream and visions of his head on his bed. Then he wrote the dream and told the sum of the matters.
